utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I might have made a different unwarranted assumption, but rather than explore that I'll refine the question. Thank you, Your Honour, for drawing my attention to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Which prison do you say that your two arrested cousins whom you have named were detained in, I think you said for about three hours, two or three hours, you said?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: The police station at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you say that they were never taken to prison in Sarajevo, do you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I put it to you that that's untrue, that they were arrested and taken to the central prison in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: May I be allowed to comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You may be allowed to answer the question, Mr. Crncalo. That's your privilege.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: The fact that you're asking me about this, I can say with certainty that that -- that they were never taken to prison in Sarajevo. The fact that they were in prison those two people, the two names that I gave you, they were together with 17 others and they were detained in the police station at Pale for two and a half to three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Then do you have any other cousins who were arrested in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: I don't know. I do have cousins, but I don't know that they were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When you were yourself arrested - you described that this morning - you were in fact carrying a rifle at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I haven't checked, Your Honour. I think that misstates his testimony. He says the house was -- it was leaning against the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I -- it's -- it's not misstating his testimony, Your Honour. It's putting that to him. That's my case. It's not misstating -- I'm not saying that he acknowledged that. I'm putting it to him now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You didn't say that you testified that, but you said -- Mr. Crncalo, Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I could see -- may I just interject. I think it's the way the question came across. It's come across on the transcript as: When you were yourself arrested, you described that this morning you were in fact carrying a rifle at the time, weren't you. I don't think that's quite what I said and I certainly didn't mean to. It was: When you were arrested, as you described this morning, I put it to you, Mr. Crncalo, that contrary to what you said this morning, you were in fact carrying a rifle.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN CRNCALO
utterances.text: It was leaning up against the wall of the house. I didn't have it in my hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be convenient to leave it leaning there overnight now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Because I see the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would even leave it there until tomorrow morning, 9.00. Mr. Crncalo, tomorrow we'll continue at 9.00. We'll be in another courtroom. We'll be in Courtroom I. I instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given, and of course you're still expected to give further testimony tomorrow. Don't speak with anyone about it, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00. We -- may I ask Madam Usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. Mr. Stewart, could you already inform us on whether you need the original of that document to be kept or would you rather ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we suggest it would be -- we said we didn't think we needed it ourselves but we suggest that it would be sensible for the original to be retained by the Court for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We do that for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would you please inform us then by tomorrow whether you think you would further need it. Otherwise I'd like to give it back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour. Well, there's no problem. If the witness has it in Court anyway if the question arises on the original, it will be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I guided Mr. Hannis that sometimes we went into details of which it was not always perfectly clear to the Chamber what these details would add to the presentation of then the Prosecutor's case. I would like to give you a similar guidance, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Hannis, any further matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, regarding scheduling, we only have one more witness scheduled for these seven days, but that's a witness who is not scheduled to arrive until Saturday, to be put on Monday. So what I'm telling the Court is that when we finish Mr. Crncalo tomorrow, we have no other witness for this week. For purpose of scheduling, I don't know if the Court wants to finish with Mr. Crncalo and then finish or if we want to talk about reading in some 92 bis summaries, going through the exhibit list, talking about reviving Rule 92 bis reviews since our pilot project on agreed facts is no longer in place, some of those housekeeping matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to get rid of a lot of matters that are still pending, such as exhibits, like the Sanski Most exhibits are all still there. Reading into the transcript, you indicated that already in your schedule. On the other hand, the Chamber is a bit disappointed that you underestimated your own ability to work quicker than scheduled. I'm afraid I can't change that at this very moment, but it's certainly not that we start in time that you would be surprised that we're running out of witnesses. That saves only a couple of minutes. But we're not only happy with this situation, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. We will try to do a better job. I think we're learning as we're going and we're -- and, for example, we had one witness that there was no cross-examination on and I have no quarrel with that. I think that was appropriate. But it's hard to estimate when that may or may not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you can't foresee everything, but even if that cross-examination would have taken one or two hours, then we still would have been, I would say, mainly in the same situation, but then for two hours less, this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I say, Your Honour, it's -- we have a great deal of sympathy with the Prosecution on this because it is terribly difficult to estimate these things. It's just that we will all do our professional best, but it seems a little bit hard, not much of an incentive to us to operate efficiently when -- when we do operate efficiently then we're subjected to criticism that time has been wasted because -- that's actually what the Prosecution, and we hope we've done the same. That's what the Prosecution have achieved with respect to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least you have additional time out of court to do other things than to listen to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Which is very valuable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm aware of that. We will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of September 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
